newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas down on Taiwan award.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas down on Taiwan award.

text.p: Gasoline prices in Singapore fell amid weaker crude and a bearish tender award by Taiwan, traders said on Tuesday.
"It is not a good impact," said one trader. "The price is lower than the last award and CPC only took one cargo."

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought by tender 250,000 barrels of unleaded 95-octane reformate cargo at $24.92 per barrel, c-and-f, for July 1-15 delivery from a U.S. major, traders said.
In its last tender which closed May 5, CPC purchased two unleaded 95-octane reformate cargoes for June 11-30 delivery at around $25.30 per barrel, c-and-f.
Traders had also expected CPC to buy at least two cargoes for June 11-30 and July 1-15 delivery to the ports of Keelung or Taichung in the tender which closed May 19 and was valid for one day.
CPC had also a very good response with over 10 companies participating, a company official said.
Talk in the Singapore fob market was thin, with only one offer was heard at $24.30 per barrel for June lifting 95-octane unleaded gasoline.
Spot naphtha prices edged down with crude with June swaps quoted at $21.90/$22.10 per barrel, down from $22.10/$22.20 on Monday.
Term talks with Saudi Aramco made progress with some Asian buyers accepting Saudi Aramco's term price for A-180 paraffinic naphtha lifting July 1997-June 1998, traders said.
But other potential buyers might drop out or have volumes cut amid difficulties in accepting Aramco's price for full-range naphtha, they said.

"Most firms in the talks are likely to have accepted the $17 per tonne premium (over the Aramco formula) for A-180 ahead of May 21 validity date," a Japanese trader said on the tender which closed April 4.

Traders said two existing term holders have agreed to the A-180 premium, and two newcomers have agreed to take up a package of A-180 and full-range naphtha at $17.00 and $15.00 per tonne respectively.
Talks held in Singapore last week had reached a deadlock by Friday, with buyers willing to meet Aramco's record high $17 target offer for the A-180 ethylene-rich feedstock from Ras Tanura.
But they were not willing to agree to the $15-premium for the low-paraffinic full-range material from Jubail and Rabigh.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
